To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flow characteristics of the impinging-jet based microburst simulator are well simulated by the microburst simulator, which is capable of generating a realistic flow field of microburst-like winds with a wide range of wind speed and wind direction, which can be used for the study of flow-structure interaction of microburst-like-wind with buildings and other structures.

the surface pressure distributions, the resultant aerodynamic forces acting upon the gable-roofs, and the flow structures around the gable-rooftop models are significantly influenced by the microburst-like flow field.

the surface pressure distributions and resultant wind loads (aerodynamic forces) acting a gable-roofed building model mounted in the core region of a microburst-like wind are much greater than those induced by a conventional wind.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the flow field measurements and wind load assessment of gable-roofed buildings in the microburst wind environment, which will provide a better understanding of the flow features of microburst-like winds, and will help us to improve our ability to accurately predict the resultant wind loads on buildings in the microbursts.
the aerodynamic characteristics of gable-roof structures in the microburst wind environment.
the flow characteristics of the microburst winds and resultant wind loads on gabled-roof building models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microburst-like impinging wind can induce significantly greater aerodynamic forces acting downward on the building models compared to the conventional atmospheric boundary layer wind.

microburst-like winds can induce considerably greater wind loads acting on buildings than conventional atmospheric boundary layer wind, and the resultant wind forces acting on gable-roofs are highly dependent on the distance of the buildings from the center of microburst-like winds, the roof angles of the buildings, and the orientations of the buildings with respect to the radial outflow direction of microburst-like air flows.
microburst-like wind is a very different flow field from the conventional atmospheric boundary layer wind.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the flow characteristics and the resultant wind loadings acting on the low-rise, gabled-roof buildings induced under the microburst-like conditions were found to be considerably different from those predicted by AS CE 7-05 wind loading standard.

the flow field and wind load measurements on the building models mounted within the core regions of the simulated microburst-like wind revealed that the building models were subjected to considerably greater aerodynamic forces than those predicted by the ASCE 7 standard.
a building placed in the core region of a microburst-like wind would be subjected to significantly higher aerodynamic forces than the forces predicted by the current wind engineering design codes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current design standards (i.e., ASCE 7) for wind-resistant building design are not adequate for predicting the wind loads acting on buildings induced by violent winds such as microburst winds, and thus, more accurate design standards are needed to ensure the structural integrity of buildings during extreme wind events.
the microburst-like flow field is very different from the conventional wind, especially in the core region of microburst-like winds.
the ASCE 7 standard may not be adequate for predicting wind loads on buildings in a microburst environment, and that the ASCE standards should be modified for use in microburst-like winds.
